sampling_model.design: Independent sampling of complete recorded trajectories from a finite-horizon behavior process.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent trajectories with one multinomial cell in \(\mathcal O\) per trajectory.
sampling_model.treatment: Actions are generated by the known recorded-history behavior policy \(\mu\). The fixed deployment rule \(\pi\) is an oracle complete-information policy when it uses latent rewards; deployment requires a separately supplied reward-recovery or sensing mechanism.
sampling_model.overlap: \(\mu_t(a\mid H_t^O)\ge\epsilon>0\) on every finite history-action cell.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The observed multinomial law is inverted jointly for validity. Fixed-law value images are computed by exact real quantifier elimination over latent trajectory probabilities; the KL confidence fiber is not represented as a polynomial program.

tldr: Finite-horizon off-policy value with MNAR discrete rewards is the image of a compact semialgebraic full-history fiber. The sole headline target remains an exact \(H=2\), binary-action, three-reward generic strict-containment result: a coefficient-complete observed table, rational completion parameterization, observable elimination minors with a nonempty relatively open sign region, an exact witness, and the exceptional equality variety. Compact attainment, common-face geometry, and fixed-law exact elimination remain supporting results. The one-stage Chen sanity proposition is now discharged by an explicit cellwise bijection, exact value-image calculation, endpoint formula, and a locally proved full-column-rank singleton lemma.

project_justification.gap: Static weak-shadow linear programs do not characterize dynamic compatibility when latent reward completion changes later oracle-policy occupancy. Iyengar's rectangular robust dynamic program assumes the product structure that an MNAR observed-data inverse fiber need not possess.
project_justification.niche: The missing theorem-level object is a checkable, coefficient-complete, relatively open region on which the exact two-stage inverse fiber has a strict endpoint gap from its stagewise product-of-projections relaxation.
project_justification.fill: The project makes the exact two-stage generic strict-containment dossier the sole headline obligation. Compact attainment, common-face geometry, the proved one-stage Chen reduction, and fixed-law quantifier elimination serve as supporting results; the one-stage result now includes a complete odds parameterization and an explicit local proof of the rank-to-singleton implication.

related_work: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong (2026), in arXiv:2602.16061v1, the source section titled Partial Identification via Linear Programs, give the matrix program at equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\) and the full-column-rank conclusion at proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\). The proved one-stage sanity proposition recovers that program under the substitutions \(X=(S_1,A_1)\), \(F=S_2\), \(Y=R_1\), and response indicator \(M_1\); its local node \(\mathrm{prop{:}point\text{-}id\text{-}mean}\) proves the required rank implication, so the source label is no longer a dangling proof dependency. No static novelty is claimed. Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1, p. 261, derives the finite-horizon Bellman recursion under rectangular ambiguity. By contrast, the still-open strict-containment question asks whether the present inverse observed-data fiber is strictly nonrectangular on a relatively open set. Wang, Xu, Lu, and Song (2025) identify and estimate MNAR OPE values through a response model and inverse weighting. Wei, Qu, and Miao (2026) use a current-state exclusion, bridge conditions, and completeness to point identify finite-horizon value. Their current-state exclusion neither implies nor is implied by \(S_{t+1}\perp M_t\mid(H_t^F,A_t,R_t)\) without additional Markov or sufficiency conditions. Duarte et al. (2024) inform certified optimization for finite discrete causal models. Chen, Christensen, and Tamer (2018) inform set-level inversion. Bennett et al. (2026) and Li, Miao, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2023) study functionals under nuisance nonuniqueness, but their static operator arguments do not address latent-history-dependent continuation occupancy.
technical_internal_limitation: Generic strict containment is not asserted until the single open obligation prints the entire two-stage rational table, affine completion map, coefficient-expanded minors, strict sign region, exact witness, and exceptional equality variety. The maintained exclusion fails when recording changes subsequent care or shares residual causes with next-state innovation. A complete-information policy is operationally unavailable without a reward-recovery or sensing mechanism. The identified value image need not be an interval because the weak-shadow fiber can be nonconvex, so fixed-law computation retains every connected component. The exact multinomial confidence fiber is not claimed to have a polynomial encoding.
honest_scope: Compactness, endpoint attainment, the supporting compact-face identity, fixed-law real quantifier elimination, and the one-stage Chen reduction have direct proofs. The one-stage result is an exact, non-novel sanity equivalence: cellwise response positivity yields a bijection between the full-history fiber and the product of Chen odds programs; this gives the sharp value image and attained weighted endpoint sums, while the locally proved node \(\mathrm{prop{:}point\text{-}id\text{-}mean}\) supplies the full-column-rank singleton implication. The sole headline remains the exact \(H=2\) generic strict-containment open obligation; the required coefficient-complete table, observable sign certificate, relatively open region, exact witness, and equality variety are not treated as established. Iyengar's Section 2, Theorem 2.1, is a comparator that assumes rectangular ambiguity; it does not prove rectangularity for an inverse observed-data fiber. The full-history exclusion is maintained rather than inherited from either static Chen conditions or Wei, Qu, and Miao's current-state exclusion. A latent-reward-dependent \(\pi\) is an oracle target unless implementation is separately supplied.

definitions.name: Full-history weak-shadow compatible-law fiber
definitions.construction:
\[
\mathcal K(p)=\left\{q\in\Delta(\Omega):
\begin{array}{ll}
O_\#q=p, & \\
q_t^F(h,a)=\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h))\displaystyle\sum_{a'\in\mathcal A}q_t^F(h,a')
&\forall (t,h,a)\in\mathcal T\times\mathcal H_t^F\times\mathcal A,\\
q_t(h,a,r,1,s)q_t(h,a,r,0,s')
=q_t(h,a,r,0,s)q_t(h,a,r,1,s')
&\forall (t,h,a,r,s,s')\in
\mathcal T\times\mathcal H_t^F\times\mathcal A\times\mathcal R\times\mathcal S^2
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
Here \(O_t:\mathcal H_t^F\to\mathcal H_t^O\) is the history-level restriction of the coarsening map \(O\).

definitions.name: Continuation-weighted stage value under full-history logging
definitions.construction:
For every \(t\in\mathcal T\),
\[
\ell_t(q)=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q(\omega)\rho_t^\pi(\omega)R_t(\omega)
=\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q(\omega)
\left\{\prod_{u=1}^t
\frac{\pi_u(A_u(\omega)\mid H_u^F(\omega))}
{\mu_u(A_u(\omega)\mid O_u(H_u^F(\omega)))}\right\}R_t(\omega),
\]
where \(O_u(H_u^F(\omega))=H_u^O(\omega)\).

definitions.name: Observed-cell Chen program for the one-stage reduction
definitions.construction: For \(H=1\), \(S_2\) plays the role of Chen's always-observed \(F\). For each \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\), set \(A_{s,a}[s',r]=p(M_1=1,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\) and \(\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=p(M_1=0,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\). Then \(\mathcal W_{s,a}=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\}\) and \(\mathcal J_{s,a}=\{\mathbf 1^\top A_{s,a}\operatorname{diag}((r)_{r\in\mathcal R})(w+\mathbf 1):w\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\}\).

definitions.name: Correctly continuation-weighted stagewise Chen projection
definitions.construction: For every \(t\in\mathcal T\), \(I_t(p)=\{\ell_t(q):q\in\mathcal K(p)\}\), \(\ell_t^-(p)=\min I_t(p)\), and \(\ell_t^+(p)=\max I_t(p)\).

definitions.name: Product-of-projections value relaxation
definitions.construction: \(\Theta^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\{\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}x_t:x_t\in I_t(p)\}\), with endpoint pair \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\ell_t^-(p)\) and \(U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}\ell_t^+(p)\).

definitions.name: Simultaneous extremizing-face systems
definitions.construction: For \(\sigma\in\{-,+\}\), \(F_t^-(p)=\{q\in\mathcal K(p):\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^-(p)\}\), \(F_t^+(p)=\{q\in\mathcal K(p):\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^+(p)\}\), and \(\mathfrak F^\sigma(p)=\bigcap_{t\in\mathcal T}F_t^\sigma(p)\).

definitions.name: Exact simultaneous multinomial confidence fiber
definitions.construction: \(C_{n,\alpha}=\{p'\in\Delta(\mathcal O):2nD_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat p_n\Vert p')\le c_{n,\alpha}(p')\}\), where \(c_{n,\alpha}(p')\) is the smallest \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile under \(n\widehat p_n\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(n,p')\) and the conventions are \(0\log(0/x)=0\) and \(x\log(x/0)=+\infty\) for \(x>0\).

definitions.name: Common-policy confidence-fiber image
definitions.construction:
For fixed common behavior and deployment kernels \(\mu\) and \(\pi\),
\[
\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}
=\bigcup_{\substack{p'\in C_{n,\alpha}\\ \mathcal K(p')\ne\varnothing}}
\Theta_I(p').
\]
The compatibility restriction only removes empty summands, because \(\Theta_I(p')=\varnothing\) whenever \(\mathcal K(p')=\varnothing\).

definitions.name: Fixed-law certified value-image elimination
definitions.construction: For fixed rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\), apply \(\mathsf{CAD}_\eta\) to the first-order real formula \(\exists q\,[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)]\); isolate every real boundary root exactly, or stop root isolation after disjoint rational intervals of width at most \(\eta\) have been certified.

definitions.name: Exact two-stage elimination dossier handle
definitions.construction: Handle: fix \(H=2\), \(S_1=s_0\), \(\mathcal S_2=\mathcal S_3=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and \(\mathcal R=\{0,1,2\}\), and write \(Y_t=M_tR_t\). Enumerate the observed table coefficient by coefficient as \(x_{a_1m_1y_1s_2a_2m_2y_2s_3}=p(A_1=a_1,M_1=m_1,Y_1=y_1,S_2=s_2,A_2=a_2,M_2=m_2,Y_2=y_2,S_3=s_3)\), where \(y_t=0\) if \(m_t=0\) and \(y_t\in\mathcal R\) if \(m_t=1\). Enumerate the complete table as \(q_{a_1r_1m_1s_2a_2r_2m_2s_3}\), impose \(x_{a_1m_1y_1s_2a_2m_2y_2s_3}=\sum_{r_1:m_1r_1=y_1}\sum_{r_2:m_2r_2=y_2}q_{a_1r_1m_1s_2a_2r_2m_2s_3}\) together with the known behavior equations, and perform exact rational row reduction to \(q=q^0(x,\mu)+B(\mu)\lambda\). Substitute this parameterization into every weak-shadow cross-product. For each observable \(2\times3\) respondent shadow block \(A\), define \(D^{ij}=A_{0i}A_{1j}-A_{0j}A_{1i}\) and \(z=(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})\); append the continuation-value coefficient row \(c(x,\mu,\pi)\) to form \(G=\det[(A_{0\cdot});(A_{1\cdot});c^\top]\). Eliminate \(\lambda\) from the cross-products, feasibility boundaries, and the two pairs of opposite stage-face optimality systems by a lexicographic Gröbner basis or resultants. The output must be a coefficient-expanded finite list \(M_j(x,\mu,\pi)\), a declared sign vector, and the corresponding common-zero ideal; names such as ``the relevant minors'' without the displayed coefficients do not complete the obligation.

statements.statement: For every \(p\) satisfying \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), the fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \(\Delta(\Omega)\), the image \(\Theta_I(p)\) is a compact semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R\), and there exist \(q^-,q^+\in\mathcal K(p)\) with \(V_\pi(q^-)=L(p)\) and \(V_\pi(q^+)=U(p)\). Every reported endpoint is therefore attained by a full trajectory law reproducing the observed cells, the known behavior factors, and all weak-shadow cross-product equations.
statements.justification: Attainment upgrades a numerical outer range into sharp policy-value endpoints supported by compatible data-generating laws.
statements.gap: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled ``Partial Identification via Linear Programs,'' equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\), establish static cellwise sharp bounds; the present compact fiber is dynamically coupled and generally nonconvex because full-history exclusion is imposed by cross-products.
statements.consumer: Clinical OPE analysts can report certified worst- and best-case deployment values without interpreting local-solver output as sharp.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(m=|\Omega|\) and \(k=|\mathcal O|\), enumerate \(\Omega=\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_m\}\) and \(\mathcal O=\{o_1,\ldots,o_k\}\), and identify a full law and an observed law with, respectively, \(q=(q_1,\ldots,q_m)\in\mathbb R^m\) and \(p=(p_1,\ldots,p_k)\in\mathbb R^k\).  The observable-data map is the fixed linear map
\[
 (O_\#q)_j=\sum_{i:O(\omega_i)=o_j}q_i,
 \qquad 1\leq j\leq k.
\tag{1}
\]
Thus the observable object is \(p=O_\#q\), whereas the causal object is the complete-law policy functional \(V_\pi(q)\).  We first verify their relationship rather than defining it into existence.

Fix \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\).  The ordinary finite-chain factorization of \(q\), together with \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\), gives on every positive-probability full-history cell
\[
 q(A_t=a\mid H_t^F=h)=\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h)).
\tag{2}
\]
Conditional kernels following zero-probability histories may be chosen arbitrarily.  Replace in this chain factorization only the action kernels in (2) by \(\pi_t(\cdot\mid h)\), leaving the initial-state and all post-action kernels fixed, and denote the resulting interventional law by \(q^\pi\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\) states that every factor \(\mu_t(a\mid g)\) is at least \(\epsilon>0\).  Induction over the finite sequence of decision stages therefore shows that every target-policy prefix having positive \(q^\pi\)-mass has positive \(q\)-mass and that, through stage \(t\), its likelihood ratio is
\[
 \prod_{u=1}^t
 \frac{\pi_u(A_u\mid H_u^F)}{\mu_u(A_u\mid H_u^O)}
 =\rho_t^\pi.
\tag{3}
\]
Indeed, the assertion is trivial before the first action; at a decision node, positivity of \(\mu_u\) preserves absolute continuity and multiplies the ratio by \(\pi_u/\mu_u\), while a shared post-action kernel leaves the ratio unchanged.  Marginalizing all variables after \(R_t\) in the two finite chain factorizations and using (3) gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{q^\pi}[R_t]
 =\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q(\omega)\rho_t^\pi(\omega)R_t(\omega)
 =\ell_t(q).
\tag{4}
\]
Consequently, by \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{q^\pi}\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^H R_t\right]
 =\sum_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)=V_\pi(q).
\tag{5}
\]
Thus \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\) takes the image of a causal full-law functional over the laws compatible with the observed distribution; it is not an observed-law regression functional.

We next use finite-dimensional closed-set algebra.  The simplex
\[
 \Delta(\Omega)=\left\{q\in\mathbb R^m:q_i\geq0\ (1\leq i\leq m),\ \sum_{i=1}^m q_i=1\right\}
\tag{6}
\]
is closed and bounded.  Every cylinder marginal \(q_t(h,a,r,m',s')\) and \(q_t^F(h,a)\) is a finite linear combination of coordinates of \(q\).  Hence (1) gives finitely many linear observed-cell equations, the full-history behavior equations in \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\) are linear, and every cross-product equation in \(\mathrm{ass{:}weak\text{-}shadow}\) is polynomial of degree at most two.  All index sets are finite.  It follows from \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}fiber}\) that \(\mathcal K(p)\) is a closed semialgebraic subset of (6).  Therefore it is compact; it is nonempty by \(\mathrm{ass{:}model\text{-}compatibility}\).

For fixed \(\pi\) and \(\mu\), define
\[
 c_i=\sum_{t=1}^H\rho_t^\pi(\omega_i)R_t(\omega_i),
 \qquad 1\leq i\leq m.
\tag{7}
\]
The reward alphabet is finite, and \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\) makes every denominator in (3) at least \(\epsilon\), so every \(c_i\) is a finite real number.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\),
\[
 V_\pi(q)=\sum_{i=1}^m c_iq_i,
\tag{8}
\]
which is linear and continuous.  Its graph over the fiber,
\[
 \Gamma_p=\left\{(q,v)\in\mathbb R^{m+1}:q\in\mathcal K(p),\ v-\sum_{i=1}^m c_iq_i=0\right\},
\tag{9}
\]
is semialgebraic.  The Tarski--Seidenberg projection theorem \(\mathrm{lem{:}tarski\text{-}seidenberg\text{-}projection}\), applied to the projection of (9) onto its last coordinate, gives
\[
 \{v:\exists q\ ((q,v)\in\Gamma_p)\}=\Theta_I(p)
\tag{10}
\]
as a semialgebraic subset of \(\mathbb R\).  This qualitative projection step permits arbitrary fixed real coefficients; in the real-algebraic case the effective version is also supplied by \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\).  Equation (10) is compact because it is the continuous image under (8) of the compact set \(\mathcal K(p)\).

Finally, a continuous real-valued function on a nonempty compact set attains its minimum and maximum.  Therefore there are \(q^-,q^+\in\mathcal K(p)\) such that
\[
 V_\pi(q^-)=\min_{q\in\mathcal K(p)}V_\pi(q)=L(p),
 \qquad
 V_\pi(q^+)=\max_{q\in\mathcal K(p)}V_\pi(q)=U(p),
\tag{11}
\]
where the final equalities are \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoints}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}fiber}\), membership of these witnesses means precisely nonnegativity and normalization, reproduction of every observed cell, satisfaction of the known full-history behavior factors, and satisfaction of every weak-shadow cross-product, including boundary cells.  Hence (11) gives attained sharp endpoints of the full compatible-law image, not merely an outer interval.

statements.statement: Supporting compact-face lemma. For every nonempty compact fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\), \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\le L(p)\le U(p)\le U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\). Moreover, \(L(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) if and only if \(\mathfrak F^-(p)\ne\varnothing\), and \(U(p)=U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) if and only if \(\mathfrak F^+(p)\ne\varnothing\). Empty common minimizing or maximizing faces therefore imply, respectively, \(\Delta^-(p)>0\) or \(\Delta^+(p)>0\).
statements.justification: This compact-set identity supplies the geometric criterion used by the strict-containment obligation; it is supporting machinery, not a headline result.
statements.gap: The identity is an elementary min-of-a-sum fact on a compact set, so no field-level novelty is claimed.
statements.consumer: The exact two-stage analysis can certify strict containment by proving that one of the two common-face intersections is empty.
statements.proof_tex:
The proof uses the elementary minimum-of-a-sum inequality and its equality condition.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}attainment}\), the nonempty fiber \(\mathcal K(p)\) is compact.  Equation (8) in that theorem also shows that each \(\ell_t\) is continuous and linear, so every stagewise minimum and maximum in \(\mathrm{def{:}stagewise\text{-}projection}\) is finite and attained.

For every \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\) and \(t\in\mathcal T\),
\[
 \ell_t^-(p)\leq \ell_t(q)\leq \ell_t^+(p).
\tag{12}
\]
Summing (12) over the finite stage set and using \(V_\pi(q)=\sum_t\ell_t(q)\), \(\mathrm{def{:}rectangular\text{-}relaxation}\), and \(\mathrm{def{:}endpoints}\) gives
\[
 L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\leq L(p)\leq U(p)\leq U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p).
\tag{13}
\]

If \(\mathfrak F^-(p)\neq\varnothing\), choose \(q_0\in\mathfrak F^-(p)\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}extremizing\text{-}faces}\), \(\ell_t(q_0)=\ell_t^-(p)\) for every \(t\), and hence
\[
 V_\pi(q_0)=\sum_t\ell_t^-(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p).
\tag{14}
\]
Together with (13), this proves \(L(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\).  Conversely, suppose that equality holds and let \(q^-\) attain \(L(p)\), as supplied by \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}attainment}\).  Define
\[
 d_t=\ell_t(q^-)-\ell_t^-(p)\geq0.
\tag{15}
\]
Then
\[
 0=L(p)-L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)=\sum_{t\in\mathcal T}d_t.
\tag{16}
\]
Because (16) is a finite sum of nonnegative real numbers, every \(d_t=0\).  Thus \(q^-\in F_t^-(p)\) for every \(t\), and \(q^-\in\mathfrak F^-(p)\).  We have proved
\[
 L(p)=L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathfrak F^-(p)\neq\varnothing.
\tag{17}
\]

Apply the same argument to an attained maximizer \(q^+\), using the nonnegative quantities \(d_t^+=\ell_t^+(p)-\ell_t(q^+)\), to obtain
\[
 U(p)=U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathfrak F^+(p)\neq\varnothing.
\tag{18}
\]
By \(\mathrm{def{:}rectangularity\text{-}defect}\), (13) implies \(\Delta^-(p)\geq0\) and \(\Delta^+(p)\geq0\).  If the corresponding intersection in (17) or (18) is empty, the respective endpoint equality is false; the associated weak inequality in (13) is then strict.  This proves \(\Delta^-(p)>0\) or \(\Delta^+(p)>0\), respectively.

statements.statement: Sanity Corollary (one-stage Chen reduction). Let \(H=1\), suppose \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), and let \(S_2\) play Chen's always-observed \(F\) role. For every \(s\) with \(p(S_1=s)>0\) and every \(a\in\mathcal A\), behavior positivity implies \(p(S_1=s,A_1=a)>0\). In each such cell define the observed respondent matrix and nonrespondent vector from the observed reward, response, and shadow table by \(A_{s,a}[s',r]=p(M_1=1,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\) and \(\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s']=p(M_1=0,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)\). Suppose cellwise response positivity holds: \(\sum_{s'\in\mathcal S}A_{s,a}[s',r]>0\) for every \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\). Then the global fiber decomposes cellwise as \(\mathcal K(p)\cong\prod_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}\mathcal W_{s,a}\), where \(\mathcal W_{s,a}=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\}\), and its value image is \(\Theta_I(p)=\{\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\theta_{s,a}:\theta_{s,a}\in\mathcal J_{s,a}\}\). Hence the endpoints are the corresponding weighted sums of the Chen cell-program endpoints. If every positive-mass cell matrix satisfies the precise full-column-rank condition \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\), necessarily with \(|\mathcal S|\ge|\mathcal R|\), then feasibility makes every \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) a singleton and the one-stage value is point identified. This is the cell program of Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong, arXiv:2602.16061v1, source section titled \emph{Partial Identification via Linear Programs}, equation label \(\texttt{opt:mnar-with-shadow-matrix-form-theta}\), and proposition label \(\texttt{prop:point-id-mean}\).
statements.justification: The proposition is a non-novel but exact regression check: it derives the static observed-cell odds programs from the one-stage full-history compatibility restrictions and maps their conditional means into the policy value.
statements.gap: Chen, Simchi-Levi, and Xiong provide the static matrix program and rank conclusion; the present proof supplies the explicit fiber bijection, handles respondent zero entries under cellwise response positivity, and derives the behavior-policy weighting.
statements.consumer: Existing static weak-shadow software can verify the one-stage specialization of the dynamic implementation cell by cell.
statements.proof_tex:
The proof uses cross-product algebra to obtain an odds parameterization, an inverse construction to establish sharpness, and importance-ratio cancellation to calculate the target value.  Put
\[
 c_{sa}=p(S_1=s,A_1=a).
\tag{19}
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}model\text{-}compatibility}\) supplies \(\bar q\in\mathcal K(p)\).  Because \(H=1\), \(H_1^F=H_1^O=S_1\).  Observed marginalization and the corrected full-history equation in \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}factorization}\) give
\[
 c_{sa}=\bar q_1^F(s,a)
 =\mu_1(a\mid s)\sum_{a'\in\mathcal A}\bar q_1^F(s,a')
 =\mu_1(a\mid s)p(S_1=s).
\tag{20}
\]
If \(p(S_1=s)>0\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\) yields
\[
 c_{sa}\geq\epsilon p(S_1=s)>0.
\tag{21}
\]
Thus every action above a positive-mass state belongs to \(\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\), while every cell above a zero-mass state has zero mass under each compatible law.

Fix \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\) and \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\).  The division in the following definitions is justified by (21):
\[
 a_{sa}(s',r)=q(M_1=1,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a),
\quad
 b_{sa}(s',r)=q(M_1=0,S_2=s',R_1=r\mid S_1=s,A_1=a).
\tag{22}
\]
By \(O_\#q=p\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}static\text{-}chen\text{-}cell\text{-}program}\),
\[
 a_{sa}(s',r)=A_{s,a}[s',r],
 \qquad
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}b_{sa}(s',r)=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}[s'].
\tag{23}
\]
Dividing the unconditional cross-products in \(\mathrm{ass{:}weak\text{-}shadow}\) by \(c_{sa}^2>0\) gives, for all \(u,s'\in\mathcal S\) and \(r\in\mathcal R\),
\[
 a_{sa}(u,r)b_{sa}(s',r)=b_{sa}(u,r)a_{sa}(s',r).
\tag{24}
\]
Define
\[
 d_{sa,r}=\sum_{u\in\mathcal S}a_{sa}(u,r),
 \qquad
 e_{sa,r}=\sum_{u\in\mathcal S}b_{sa}(u,r).
\tag{25}
\]
The proposition's cellwise response-positivity condition and (23) imply \(d_{sa,r}>0\).  Summing (24) over \(u\) and dividing only by this positive column total gives
\[
 b_{sa}(s',r)=a_{sa}(s',r)w_{sa,r},
 \qquad
 w_{sa,r}=e_{sa,r}/d_{sa,r}\geq0.
\tag{26}
\]
No individual entry of \(A_{s,a}\) is divided by; in particular, (26) forces the matching nonrespondent entry to vanish when a respondent entry is zero.  Summing (26) over \(r\) and using (23) gives
\[
 A_{s,a}w_{sa}=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a},
\tag{27}
\]
so \(w_{sa}\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\).  Moreover, (26) shows that \(w_{sa}\) uniquely determines, and is uniquely determined by, the conditional completion in this cell.  Hence there is an injective map
\[
 \Phi:\mathcal K(p)\longrightarrow
 \prod_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}\mathcal W_{s,a}.
\tag{28}
\]

For surjectivity, choose any family \((w_{sa})\) in the product in (28), and on each positive cell define
\[
 q^w(R_1=r,M_1=1,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)=A_{s,a}[s',r],
\tag{29}
\]
\[
 q^w(R_1=r,M_1=0,S_2=s'\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)=A_{s,a}[s',r]w_{sa,r}.
\tag{30}
\]
Feasibility (27) implies that the total conditional mass in (29)--(30) equals
\[
 \sum_{s',r}A_{s,a}[s',r](1+w_{sa,r})
 =p(M_1=1\mid S_1=s,A_1=a)+\mathbf 1^\top\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}=1.
\tag{31}
\]
Give this conditional distribution baseline mass \(c_{sa}\), and assign zero mass to cells above states with \(p(S_1=s)=0\).  Equations (29), (30), and (27) reproduce every observed respondent and nonrespondent cell, so \(O_\#q^w=p\).  Equation (20), which is a necessary observable implication of nonempty compatibility, verifies the full-history behavior equation for \(q^w\).  For fixed \((s,a,r)\), the response-one and response-zero vectors over \(s'\) are \(A_{s,a}[s',r]\) and \(A_{s,a}[s',r]w_{sa,r}\).  Therefore, for every \(u,s'\),
\[
 A_{s,a}[u,r]A_{s,a}[s',r]w_{sa,r}
 =A_{s,a}[u,r]w_{sa,r}A_{s,a}[s',r].
\tag{32}
\]
Multiplication by \(c_{sa}^2\) verifies the weak-shadow cross-products, including zero entries and zero baseline cells.  Thus \(q^w\in\mathcal K(p)\), and (26), (29), and (30) show that this construction is inverse to \(\Phi\).  Consequently
\[
 \mathcal K(p)\cong
 \prod_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}\mathcal W_{s,a}.
\tag{33}
\]

It remains to calculate the target functional.  By \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\), positivity makes the denominator below nonzero, and (20), (26), and (29)--(30) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 V_\pi(q)
 &=\sum_{s,a,r,m,s'}q(s,a,r,m,s')
   \frac{\pi_1(a\mid s)}{\mu_1(a\mid s)}r\\
 &=\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}
   \frac{c_{sa}\pi_1(a\mid s)}{\mu_1(a\mid s)}
   \sum_{s',r}rA_{s,a}[s',r](1+w_{sa,r})\\
 &=\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}
   p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\theta_{s,a},
\end{aligned}
\tag{34}
\]
where, by \(\mathrm{def{:}static\text{-}chen\text{-}cell\text{-}program}\),
\[
 \theta_{s,a}=\mathbf 1^\top A_{s,a}
 \operatorname{diag}((r)_{r\in\mathcal R})(w_{sa}+\mathbf 1)
 \in\mathcal J_{s,a}.
\tag{35}
\]
Conversely, every independent choice \(\theta_{s,a}\in\mathcal J_{s,a}\) has a witnessing \(w_{sa}\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\), and (29)--(32) paste all such witnesses into one compatible law.  Combining this fact with \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\) proves the exact image
\[
 \Theta_I(p)=\left\{
 \sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\theta_{s,a}:
 \theta_{s,a}\in\mathcal J_{s,a}
 \right\}.
\tag{36}
\]

The extrema in (36) are attained.  Indeed, (27) implies
\[
 \sum_{r\in\mathcal R}d_{sa,r}w_{sa,r}
 =\mathbf 1^\top\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}.
\tag{37}
\]
Since every \(d_{sa,r}>0\), each feasible coordinate obeys
\[
 0\leq w_{sa,r}\leq
 \frac{\mathbf 1^\top\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}}{d_{sa,r}}.
\tag{38}
\]
Thus each nonempty \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) is a compact convex polytope and \(\mathcal J_{s,a}\) is a compact interval.  The weights in (36) are nonnegative, so independent cellwise extremization gives
\[
 L(p)=\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\min\mathcal J_{s,a},
 \qquad
 U(p)=\sum_{(s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)}p(S_1=s)\pi_1(a\mid s)\max\mathcal J_{s,a}.
\tag{39}
\]
These are sharp bounds, because every simultaneous choice was realized in (29)--(32).

Finally, if \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\) in every positive cell, then necessarily \(|\mathcal S|\geq|\mathcal R|\).  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal K(p)\) and (28) make every \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) nonempty.  Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}point\text{-}id\text{-}mean}\) therefore makes each \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\), and hence each \(\mathcal J_{s,a}\), a singleton.  Equation (36) is then a singleton.  Under \(X=(S_1,A_1)\), \(F=S_2\), \(Y=R_1\), and response indicator \(M_1\), equations (27), (35), and (39) are the advertised static Chen cell program and its full-column-rank implication.

statements.statement: Sole headline open obligation (exact two-stage generic strict containment). Execute \(\mathrm{def{:}strictness\text{-}handle}\) on the model \(H=2\), \(S_1=s_0\), \(\mathcal S_2=\mathcal S_3=\{0,1\}\), \(\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and \(\mathcal R=\{0,1,2\}\). The deliverable is one coefficient-complete algebraic dossier satisfying all of the following requirements: (i) list every rational observed atom \(x_{a_1m_1y_1s_2a_2m_2y_2s_3}\), every rational behavior and oracle-policy probability, the complete affine parameterization \(q=q^0+B\lambda\), and every feasible interval or semialgebraic constraint on \(\lambda\); (ii) display every \(D^{ij}\), every continuation determinant \(G\), every elimination polynomial \(M_j(x,\mu,\pi)\), and one explicit strict sign vector; (iii) prove that the compatible sign region \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{strict}}=\{(x,\mu,\pi):M_j\mathrel{\triangleright_j}0\ \text{ for every listed }j\}\) is nonempty and relatively open, with each relation \(\triangleright_j\in\{>,<,\ne\}\) printed in the dossier; (iv) prove on all of \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{strict}}\) that \(\pi_2(\cdot\mid r_1)\) differs for at least two latent rewards and that \(\Delta^-(p)>0\) or \(\Delta^+(p)>0\); (v) give one cell-by-cell exact rational witness, verify normalization, observed marginalization, known behavior factors, positivity, all weak-shadow cross-products, \(A w=\boldsymbol\beta\), the null directions, and certify \(\Theta_I(p)=[229/140,26/15]\) together with exact rational \(L^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) and \(U^{\mathrm{rect}}(p)\) establishing a strict endpoint gap; and (vi) prove that, away from explicitly listed rank-degenerate and reward-history-blind policy faces, the equality locus is exactly the compatible part of the coefficient-expanded common-zero variety \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{eq}}=\mathcal V(M_j:j\in J_{\mathrm{eq}})\), with the index set \(J_{\mathrm{eq}}\) printed. Until this dossier is supplied, generic strict containment is an open question and no existence of the table, sign region, or equality characterization is asserted. Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, obtains Bellman recursion after assuming rectangular ambiguity; this obligation must instead establish strict nonrectangularity of an inverse observed-data fiber.
statements.justification: A coefficient-complete relatively open strictness region, not the compact-face identity, is the sole theorem-level novelty target.
statements.gap: Iyengar (2005), Section 2, Theorem 2.1 (finite-horizon robust Bellman equation), p. 261, assumes a rectangular product of conditional ambiguity sets to obtain robust recursion. Static weak-shadow programs do not determine whether the dynamically coupled inverse observed-data fiber is strictly nonrectangular.
statements.consumer: The printed sign certificate would let a sepsis OPE analyst detect when stagewise MNAR bounds are provably too wide for an oracle policy that reacts to latent reward history.

obligation.what_is_open: The coefficient-complete two-stage dossier remains open: no explicit rational observed atom table, affine pair \(q^0+B\lambda\), complete eliminated polynomial family \(M_j\), strict sign vector, exact endpoint calculation, or common-zero index set \(\mathcal J_{\mathrm{eq}}\) is present in the frozen core, and this solve does not derive those coefficients.
obligation.obstruction: The compact-face criterion reduces strict containment to emptiness of a simultaneous stage-face system, while the signed-minor calculation only certifies a local objective slope. It does not show that locally forced opposite boundary choices are incompatible with one globally coupled complete-history law. Establishing that incompatibility on a relatively open observable region requires carrying out the specified elimination after choosing and verifying a concrete rational witness; the symbolic handles \(q^0\), \(B\), and \(M_j\) do not themselves contain that calculation.
obligation.attempted: I reduced both endpoint gaps to exact common-face emptiness formulas, parameterized each rank-two \(2\times3\) Chen block by its signed-minor null vector, and computed the continuation slope as \(c^\top z=G\). I also checked that exact CAD decides any fixed instantiated face system. These routes stop before the required cross-stage coefficient expansion and relatively open sign certificate.
obligation.partial_result:
The frozen core does yield the following exact, computable partial characterization.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}compact\text{-}face\text{-}pasting}\),
\[
 \Delta^-(p)>0\iff
 \neg\exists q\left[q\in\mathcal K(p)\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^-(p)\right],
\]
and
\[
 \Delta^+(p)>0\iff
 \neg\exists q\left[q\in\mathcal K(p)\ \wedge\ \bigwedge_{t=1}^H\ell_t(q)=\ell_t^+(p)\right].
\]
For a fixed rational or real-algebraic observed law and policies, \(\mathrm{thm{:}fixed\text{-}law\text{-}value\text{-}image}\) makes these emptiness assertions decidable by exact real elimination after the stage endpoints have been computed.

There is also a local observable slope certificate.  For a two-row, three-reward respondent block \(A\), direct cofactor expansion gives
\[
 A(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})^\top=0.
\]
If \(A\) has rank two, this vector spans \(\ker A\).  For a continuation coefficient row \(c^\top\), another cofactor expansion gives
\[
 c^\top(D^{12},-D^{02},D^{01})^\top
 =\det[(A_{0\cdot});(A_{1\cdot});c^\top]=G.
\]
Hence, on any feasible line \(w+\lambda z\), the local continuation objective is affine with slope \(G\), and \(G\neq0\) forces a local extremum to a feasibility boundary.  What remains unproved is the global elimination step showing, on one printed relatively open sign region, that the boundary choices forced at the two stages cannot be realized by one common complete-history law.

statements.statement: For finite alphabets and fixed rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\) with \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), \(\mathsf{CAD}_\eta\) terminates on \(\exists q\,[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)]\) and returns all connected components of \(\Theta_I(p)\) as closed intervals or singleton points with exact real-algebraic endpoints; alternatively it returns disjoint certified rational \(\eta\)-enclosures of every component and endpoint. For a presentation with \(N\) real variables, \(s\) polynomial constraints, and maximum degree \(d\), classical sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition uses at most \((sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\) arithmetic operations, with exact coefficient arithmetic, and the same bound controls the number of cells examined.
statements.proof_tex:
The technique is exact sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition, using \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\) as the classical algorithmic result and deriving its specialization to this compatible-law fiber.

Fix rational or real-algebraic \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\).  By \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}positivity}\), every coordinate \(\mu_t(a\mid g)\) appearing in an importance ratio is at least \(\epsilon>0\).  Thus its reciprocal exists and is real algebraic.  The field generated over \(\mathbb Q\) by the finitely many coordinates of \(p\), \(\mu\), and \(\pi\), together with these reciprocals, is an effectively represented real-algebraic coefficient field.

Write \(q=(q_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}compatible\text{-}fiber}\), the formula \(q\in\mathcal K(p)\) is the finite conjunction of
\[
 q_\omega\geq0,
 \qquad \sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q_\omega=1,
 \qquad
 \sum_{\omega:O(\omega)=o}q_\omega=p(o)\quad(o\in\mathcal O),
\tag{40}
\]
the linear full-history behavior equations
\[
 q_t^F(h,a)-\mu_t(a\mid O_t(h))
 \sum_{a'\in\mathcal A}q_t^F(h,a')=0,
\tag{41}
\]
and the quadratic weak-shadow cross-products
\[
 q_t(h,a,r,1,s)q_t(h,a,r,0,s')
 -q_t(h,a,r,0,s)q_t(h,a,r,1,s')=0.
\tag{42}
\]
All cylinder quantities in (41)--(42) are linear sums of the \(q_\omega\).  Moreover, \(\mathrm{def{:}stage\text{-}value}\) gives the linear polynomial equation
\[
 v-\sum_{\omega\in\Omega}q_\omega
 \sum_{t=1}^H\rho_t^\pi(\omega)R_t(\omega)=0
\tag{43}
\]
for \(v=V_\pi(q)\).  Thus
\[
 \Phi(v)\;\Longleftrightarrow\;
 \exists(q_\omega)_{\omega\in\Omega}
 \bigl[q\in\mathcal K(p)\wedge v=V_\pi(q)\bigr]
\tag{44}
\]
is a first-order real formula over that coefficient field.  In the presentation fixed in the theorem, (44) has \(N\) real variables including \(v\), \(s\) polynomial equalities and weak inequalities, and maximum total degree \(d\).

Apply \(\mathrm{lem{:}effective\text{-}real\text{-}cad}\) to all polynomials in (40)--(43), with \(v\) ordered as the uneliminated coordinate.  The algorithm terminates and produces an equivalent quantifier-free univariate sign formula for \(\Phi(v)\), using exact coefficient arithmetic.  The cited CAD bound gives at most
\[
 (sd)^{2^{O(N)}}
\tag{45}
\]
arithmetic operations.  Since producing or inspecting a CAD cell requires at least one algorithmic operation, the number of cells examined is bounded by the same asymptotic quantity.

By \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\), the truth set of (44) is exactly \(\Theta_I(p)\).  A univariate quantifier-free sign formula changes truth value only at a real root of one of its finitely many nonzero projection polynomials.  Its truth set is therefore a finite union of points and intervals with real-algebraic boundary points.  By \(\mathrm{thm{:}sharp\text{-}attainment}\), \(\Theta_I(p)\) is compact, hence closed and bounded.  After adjacent true CAD cells are merged, every connected component is consequently either a singleton or a closed interval, and all endpoints are real algebraic.

For the exact output, CAD records each boundary root by a defining polynomial and exact root-identification data, such as a Thom encoding.  For the tolerance alternative, let \(E\) be the finite set of distinct component endpoints.  Exact comparison of real-algebraic numbers orders \(E\).  Because \(\eta>0\) and distinct elements of \(E\) have positive separation, repeated rational bisection of their certified isolating intervals yields pairwise disjoint rational intervals, each of width at most \(\eta\).  The defining polynomial and root-identification data certify containment even for an even-multiplicity endpoint, for which a sign-change test would fail.  Pairing the two endpoint enclosures describes each interval component; the single enclosure describes a singleton component.  This proves the stated certified \(\eta\)-description of all components and endpoints.  The procedure eliminates the entire feasible formula (40)--(44), so its certificate is global and does not rely on convexity or on the output of a local optimizer.
statements.justification: The result turns fixed-law sharpness into a terminating exact computation rather than a local numerical optimization claim.
statements.gap: Duarte et al. (2024) motivate certified polynomial optimization for discrete causal models; this theorem specializes exact real elimination to the coupled weak-shadow value image and reports all connected components.
statements.consumer: An auditor can reproduce exact algebraic policy-value bounds for a finite sepsis table or request certified enclosures at tolerance \(\eta\).

statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite family of \(s\) polynomials of maximum degree \(d\) in \(N\) real variables over an effectively represented real-algebraic coefficient field. A sign-invariant cylindrical algebraic decomposition adapted to \(\mathcal P\) can be computed, yields quantifier elimination for first-order real formulas using \(\mathcal P\), and has arithmetic complexity \((sd)^{2^{O(N)}}\).

statements.statement: For every \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\), suppose \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\ne\varnothing\) and \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\). Then \(|\mathcal S|\ge |\mathcal R|\), the feasible set \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) is a singleton, and its linear image \(\mathcal J_{s,a}\) is a singleton.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \((s,a)\in\mathcal X_{SA}(p)\). By \(\mathrm{def{:}static\text{-}chen\text{-}cell\text{-}program}\),
\[
\mathcal W_{s,a}=\{w\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal R|}:A_{s,a}w=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}\}.
\]
If \(w,w'\in\mathcal W_{s,a}\), subtraction of their defining equalities gives
\[
A_{s,a}(w-w')=\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}-\boldsymbol\beta_{s,a}=0.
\]
The hypothesis \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{s,a})=|\mathcal R|\) says that the \(|\mathcal R|\) columns are linearly independent, hence \(\ker(A_{s,a})=\{0\}\). Therefore \(w-w'=0\), so \(w=w'\). Nonemptiness then makes \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) a singleton. Since the rank of a \(|\mathcal S|\)-by-\(|\mathcal R|\) matrix is at most \(\min\{|\mathcal S|,|\mathcal R|\}\), the same rank hypothesis implies \(|\mathcal S|\ge |\mathcal R|\). Finally, \(\mathcal J_{s,a}\) is, by the same definition, the image of \(\mathcal W_{s,a}\) under the scalar-valued map
\[
w\longmapsto \mathbf 1^\top A_{s,a}\operatorname{diag}((r)_{r\in\mathcal R})(w+\mathbf 1),
\]
and the image of a singleton is a singleton.
statements.justification: This local linear-algebra proposition supplies the formerly dangling full-column-rank implication used by the one-stage reduction.
statements.gap: The published source states the same rank implication; the present node proves the exact finite-matrix fact needed by the local dependency graph.
statements.consumer: It discharges the point-identification clause of the one-stage Chen sanity corollary.

statements.statement:
Assume \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}p\), use the same fixed kernels \(\mu\) and \(\pi\) in every summand, and define the cutoff and \(C_{n,\alpha}\) as in \(\mathrm{def{:}confidence\text{-}fiber}\). Then
\[
\Pr_p\!\left\{\Theta_I(p)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\right\}
\geq \Pr_p\!\left\{p\in C_{n,\alpha}\right\}
\geq 1-\alpha.
\]
The condition \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\) is needed only to make the covered identified set nonempty. The first inequality can be strict, so the confidence-fiber image is an exact finite-sample, possibly conservative, whole-set confidence region.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(E=\{p\in C_{n,\alpha}\}\) and \(F=\{\Theta_I(p)\subseteq\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}\}\). The proof uses event inclusion and the defining multinomial quantile; it does not identify the causal target by an observed regression.

On \(E\), if \(\mathcal K(p)\ne\varnothing\), then \(p\) is one of the indices in the union in \(\mathrm{def{:}whole\text{-}set\text{-}region}\). Hence its own summand occurs and
\[
\Theta_I(p)\subseteq
\bigcup_{\substack{p'\in C_{n,\alpha}\\\mathcal K(p')\ne\varnothing}}
\Theta_I(p')=\widehat\Theta_{n,\alpha}.
\tag{1}
\]
If instead \(\mathcal K(p)=\varnothing\), then \(\mathrm{def{:}identified\text{-}set}\) gives \(\Theta_I(p)=\varnothing\), and (1) is again true. Thus \(E\subseteq F\), which proves
\[
\Pr_p(F)\geq\Pr_p(E).
\tag{2}
\]

Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}trajectories}\), \(n\widehat p_n\) has the multinomial distribution with parameters \((n,p)\). By \(\mathrm{def{:}confidence\text{-}fiber}\), the event \(E\) is
\[
2nD_{\mathrm{KL}}(\widehat p_n\Vert p)\leq c_{n,\alpha}(p).
\tag{3}
\]
The cutoff is a \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of the random variable on the left of (3) under that same multinomial law. By the defining property of a quantile, including possible atoms at the cutoff,
\[
\Pr_p(E)\geq1-\alpha.
\tag{4}
\]
Combining (2) and (4) proves the two inequalities. No equality between the two probabilities follows: values belonging to other laws in the random fiber can cover \(\Theta_I(p)\) even when \(p\notin C_{n,\alpha}\), which is the stated source of conservativeness.
statements.justification: This is the promised usable whole-set inference conclusion, rather than only a definition of a confidence-fiber image.
statements.gap: Pointwise inversion of a valid multinomial law confidence set yields simultaneous coverage of the entire true value image without selecting one latent completion.
statements.consumer: A finite-table OPE analysis can report the union image as an exact finite-sample, possibly conservative, confidence region for every value compatible with the true observed law.

\[
\{y\in\mathbb R^k:\exists x\in\mathbb R^m,\ (x,y)\in S\}
\]
is semialgebraic.
